headline: Anabolic steroids
body: Not the way the internet thinks they do.
punch: The animal data shows alteration — not enhancement.

headline: Jaw development
body: Mandibular growth, forward growth, the condyle. Most of what circulates about hormones and jaw structure is inference dressed as mechanism.
punch: There is actual data. It's in rats, and it's more complicated.

headline: Nandrolone
body: In both juvenile and adult female rats, measured by radiographic cephalometry — real morphometric measurement, not visual impression.
punch: The effect is documented. The direction is the point.

headline: The word used
body: Not increased. Not improved. Craniofacial growth responded to anabolic steroids, and the response varied by site and by whether the animal was still growing.
punch: Different bones in the same skull responded differently.

headline: That site-dependence
body: Craniofacial growth isn't one process. The mandible, the condyle and the cranial base have different growth mechanisms and different hormone sensitivities.
punch: A hormone that helps one site can distort another.

headline: And in adults
body: Effects appeared in adult animals too, not only juveniles — which means these compounds act on craniofacial bone outside the growth window as well.
punch: Adult bone is not inert to this.

headline: Why that's a warning
body: Facial harmony depends on proportion between sites. A compound that changes several sites by different amounts is more likely to distort than to improve.
punch: Changing multiple bones unevenly is not an aesthetic strategy.

headline: The evidence limits
body: Rat cephalometry, mostly female animals, supraphysiologic exposure. Rodent craniofacial growth differs substantially from human. This does not transfer cleanly.
punch: Real measurement in the wrong species is still the wrong species.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
